The application models silicate using salinity, log pressure and oxygen.
Oxygen is recorded in four bands, with exact measurements available for
0%, 20% or 50% of the training profiles. The same frozen cohort, five folds
and nested observation masks are used throughout.

## 1. Select the computation

Choose `action="plan"` to inspect the selected work, `"run"` to fit or
resume, and `"report"` to read completed fits. `folds`, `cells` and
`modules` select work without changing numerical settings or seeds.
Use separate result roots for distributed jobs and `import_dirs` to merge
compatible completed tasks. Runnable examples and all selectors are in
`codes/applications/ocean_silicate/README.md`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,cache=FALSE,error=FALSE)
input <- knitr::current_input(dir=TRUE)
repository_dir <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(input),".."),mustWork=TRUE)
source(file.path(repository_dir,"codes/applications/ocean_silicate/01_setup.R"),local=TRUE)
ocean_source_modules(repository_dir,environment())
settings <- ocean_settings(profile=params$profile,action=params$action,folds=params$folds,
  cells=params$cells,modules=params$modules,augmented_methods=params$augmented_methods,
  placeholders=params$placeholders,task_ids=params$task_ids,cores=params$cores,run_id=params$run_id)
data_dir <- if(nzchar(params$data_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$data_dir,repository_dir) else file.path(repository_dir,"data/ocean_silicate")
output_dir <- if(nzchar(params$output_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$output_dir,repository_dir) else file.path(repository_dir,"reproduction/ocean",settings$profile)
diagnostics_dir <- if(nzchar(params$diagnostics_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$diagnostics_dir,repository_dir) else file.path(output_dir,"diagnostics")
import_dirs <- as.character(unlist(params$import_dirs)); import_dirs <- import_dirs[nzchar(import_dirs)]
import_dirs <- ocean_resolve_path(import_dirs,repository_dir)
augmented_output_dir <- if(nzchar(params$augmented_output_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$augmented_output_dir,repository_dir) else ""
inputs <- ocean_prepare_inputs(data_dir)
selected <- ocean_select_tasks(settings)
```

```{r selected-work, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
cat(sprintf("**Profile:** %s; **action:** %s; **folds:** %s; **training calibration:** %s.\n\n",
  settings$profile,settings$action,paste(settings$folds,collapse=", "),
  paste(paste0(sub("O","",settings$cells),"%"),collapse=", ")))
cat(sprintf("Selected work: **%d base tasks** and **%d conditional continuation candidates**.\n\n",
  sum(selected$module!="continuation"),sum(selected$module=="continuation")))
```

Paper fits use four chains of 20,000 iterations, burn-in 5,000 and
`u_block_size=8`. A cell receives one additional 20,000 iterations when
its initial maximum finite Rhat exceeds 1.01, minimum finite bulk ESS is
below 400, or no finite values are available. Undefined diagnostics and
tail ESS are recorded for inspection. The fitting overview below combines
availability, continuation and final screening in one row per fold.
The `quick` profile uses fold 1/O0/O50 and one 80-iteration chain as a
workflow check.

## 2. Explore the observed data

The frozen subset contains 200 distinct profiles. Each fold has 160
training and 40 held-out profiles. Recorded oxygen is retained for offline
checking; only the calibration-mask entries enter the model as exact U.

```{r data-design}
cohort <- inputs$cohort
levels(cohort$oxygen_class) <- c("<50","50-100","100-150","150-180")
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(cohort$oxygen_class)),
  col.names=c("Oxygen class (micromol/kg)","Observations"))
```

```{r exploratory-plots, eval=settings$action!="plan", fig.width=10, fig.height=3.8}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(cohort,aes(U,Y,color=oxygen_class))+geom_point(alpha=.65)+
  labs(x="Measured oxygen (micromol/kg)",y="Silicate (micromol/kg)",color="Oxygen class")+
  theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="none")
p2 <- ggplot(cohort,aes(oxygen_class,Y,fill=oxygen_class))+geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha=.4)+
  labs(x="Oxygen class (micromol/kg)",y="Silicate (micromol/kg)")+
  theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="none")
p3 <- ggplot(cohort,aes(G2salinity,Y,color=log_pressure))+geom_point(alpha=.65)+
  labs(x="Salinity",y="Silicate (micromol/kg)",color="Log pressure")+theme_minimal()
p1+p2+p3
```

## 3. Fit the models and make held-out predictions

The chunk below is the workflow entry point. With `action="run"`, it fits
selected tasks or reuses verified completed tasks, checks the initial
chains, continues cells selected by those diagnostics, and saves held-out
predictions. With `action="report"`, it reads completed results; with
`action="plan"`, it returns the task plan.

```{r fit, class.source="fold-show", results="hide"}
if (settings$action == "plan") {
  analysis <- ocean_execute(repository_dir, data_dir, output_dir, settings)
} else {
  analysis <- ocean_logged(
    file.path(output_dir, "jobs", settings$run_id, "execution.log"),
    ocean_execute(
      repository_dir, data_dir, output_dir, settings,
      import_dirs = import_dirs,
      augmented_output_dir = augmented_output_dir
    )
  )
}
```

`01_setup.R` assigns the selected tasks to the fitting functions in
`02_fit_models.R`. For each EIV task, `run_eiv()` prepares X, C and U_obs,
calls `eivGP::fit_eivgp()`, then `eivGP::predict_eivgp()` and
`eivGP::impute_eivgp()`. X contains salinity and log pressure; C contains
the recorded oxygen class; U_obs contains calibration measurements and
NA elsewhere. Selected continuations call `eivGP::continue_eivgp()` and
update predictions and imputation from the continued fit.

Baseline tasks call the pinned adapter
`eivGP:::run_published_mixedgp_competitors()`, which uses `kergp::gp()`,
`LVGP::LVGP_fit()` or `EzGP::EzGP_fit()` and their native predictors.
Unstarred methods use (x,c). Starred methods add categorical observation
status R and continuous oxygen record W; observed W uses the training
calibration mean/SD, and hidden W takes placeholder 0. Native kernels and
fitting procedures are used for both representations.

```{r fitting-overview, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
ocean_fit_overview(analysis, output_dir)
```

## 4. Inspect held-out silicate predictions

The fitting module saves held-out predictions from `predict_eivgp()`,
together with posterior-state IDs and seeds for each initial or continued
fit. The table below summarizes those saved predictions.

Class-only testing supplies no exact test oxygen. Mixed testing reveals
20% or 50% under the same saved masks to EIV-GP and the starred baselines.
At those rows, EIV-GP uses `new_U` and `new_U_scale="raw"`; other rows keep
class-only predictions. All held-out responses are excluded from fitting
and tuning.

```{r prediction-table, eval=settings$action!="plan" && "prediction" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
ocean_show_predictions(analysis$prediction)
```

**Starred methods:** UC-GP*, LVGP* and EzGP* receive the same available
exact oxygen values as EIV-GP through the (x,c,R,W) encoding described above.
The primary placeholder is 0. At O0, unstarred methods use (x,c). Entries
are fold means with sample SDs; fold SD describes variation across the
overlapping training sets. CSV, Markdown, LaTeX and HTML tables are exported
beside the unrounded scores.

## 5. Inspect oxygen imputation and response functions

The following components use the final EIV fits. Full displays require
all five original baseline groups, all EIV cells and their selected
continuations. Nearby measured profiles are shown once with the m/f fits.

```{r diagnostics-build, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, include=FALSE}
diagnostics <- NULL; surfaces <- NULL; diagnostic_run <- NULL
available <- analysis$prediction
if(is.null(available)) available <- ocean_prediction_report(output_dir,inputs,"paper",augmented_output_dir)
baseline_ready <- all(vapply(1:5,function(f) file.exists(file.path(output_dir,"full5_class4",sprintf("fold%02d",f),"baseline_package_outputs.rds")),logical(1)))
if(all(available$availability$available) && baseline_ready) {
  diagnostic_run <- ocean_logged(file.path(output_dir,"jobs",settings$run_id,"diagnostics.log"),
    ocean_run_diagnostics(output_dir,data_dir,report_dir=diagnostics_dir,
      augmented_output_dir=augmented_output_dir,representative_fold=params$representative_fold,
      workers=params$diagnostics_workers,build_prediction=FALSE,prediction_report=available,
      build_surfaces="surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules))
  diagnostics <- diagnostic_run$diagnostics; surfaces <- diagnostic_run$surfaces
}
```

```{r surfaces-build, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules, include=FALSE}
if(!exists("diagnostics")) diagnostics <- NULL
if(!exists("surfaces")) surfaces <- NULL
if(is.null(surfaces) && all(file.exists(file.path(diagnostics_dir,"tables",c("m_points.csv","f_points.csv")))) &&
  all(vapply(1:5,function(f) file.exists(file.path(output_dir,"full5_class4",sprintf("fold%02d",f),"baseline_package_outputs.rds")),logical(1))))
  surfaces <- ocean_surface_report(output_dir,data_dir,diagnostics_dir,representative_fold=params$representative_fold)
```

### Training oxygen imputation

O20/O50 are scored on the same 80 hidden training rows per fold using bias,
RMSE, MAE, 95% coverage and interval width. Hollow points are measured
calibration inputs; solid points and intervals summarize masked-input
posteriors. O0 remains on its unanchored model coordinate.

```{r imputation-display, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=13.2, fig.height=6}
if(is.null(diagnostics)) cat("Imputation displays are pending complete final fits.\n") else {
  u_tables <- ocean_paper_u_tables(diagnostics$u$summary)
  cat(ocean_table_html(u_tables$main,"Training oxygen imputation",u_tables$note),"\n\n")
  print(diagnostics$plots$u_main)
}
```

### Category means m(x,c)

Category means integrate the fitted response over the conditional oxygen
distribution. The pressure slice fixes salinity at 34.20. The comparison
uses the three original (x,c) baselines; their category predictors target m
directly. EIV O0 uses class-only training information, and O20/O50 show the
calibrated fits.

```{r category-mean-display, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
if(!is.null(surfaces)) print(surfaces$plots$m_comparison) else cat("Category-mean displays are pending complete final fits.\n")
```

Points are measured silicate in the local salinity pool, balanced over
six log-pressure bins with at most three nearest-salinity profiles per bin.
Filled and hollow points identify training and held-out profiles. Selection
uses inputs only; these noisy responses provide context for the fitted means.

### Continuous response f(x,u)

The continuous slice fixes salinity at 34.25 and pressure at 650 dbar, then
varies oxygen. It uses O20/O50 fits on the physical oxygen scale. The grid
follows the central oxygen range of nearby reference profiles.

```{r continuous-surface-display, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
if(!is.null(surfaces)) print(surfaces$plots$f_with_observations) else cat("Continuous-response displays are pending calibrated final fits.\n")
```

The measured profiles have nearby, varying salinity and pressure, and their
responses include noise. Shading in both m/f plots represents pointwise
95% credible intervals for the mean, including conditional GP uncertainty.
It excludes response noise. True m/f values are unavailable in this
semi-real application, so these displays are not surface-recovery scores.

### Supplement: separate fitted folds

```{r all-fold-imputation, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules && isTRUE(params$appendix), echo=FALSE, fig.width=13.2, fig.height=14}
if(!is.null(diagnostics)) print(diagnostics$plots$u_all_folds)
```

```{r all-fold-functions, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules && isTRUE(params$appendix), echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=13}
if(!is.null(surfaces)) {
  print(surfaces$plots$m_comparison_all_folds)
  print(surfaces$plots$f_with_observations_all_folds)
}
```

```{r class-imputation-table, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules && isTRUE(params$appendix), echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
if(!is.null(diagnostics)) {
  u_tables <- ocean_paper_u_tables(diagnostics$u$summary)
  cat(ocean_table_html(u_tables$class,"Training oxygen imputation by class",u_tables$note),"\n\n")
}
```

## 6. Reproduce and cite

Seeds are independent of work assignment and execution order. Completed-task
receipts validate reuse and merging. Full diagnostics and logs are stored
under the result root; `jobs/<run_id>/` contains execution logs. The HTML
embeds its figures. Data provenance and environment requirements are in
`codes/applications/ocean_silicate/README.md`.

Data: GLODAPv2.2023 merged and adjusted product, DOI **10.25921/zyrq-ht66**.
Product reference: Lauvset et al. (2024), *Earth System Science Data* 16,
2047–2072, DOI **10.5194/essd-16-2047-2024**.

```{r environment, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(R=as.character(getRversion()),profile=settings$profile,action=settings$action))
sessionInfo()
```
